name: Contextual Experience Replay (CER): Contextual Experience Replay for Self-Improvement of Language Agents
venue: ACL 2025 (Proceedings of the 63rd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, Long Papers, pp. 14179-14198). Also released as preprint arXiv:2506.06698 (submitted 7 Jun 2025). An earlier version was submitted to ICLR 2025 under the title 'Contextual Experience Replay for Continual Learning of Language Agents' (OpenReview id RXvFK5dnpz).
authors_affiliation: Yitao Liu (Princeton University; work done while a student researcher at Princeton, now a PhD student at The University of Hong Kong / xlang-ai), Chenglei Si (Stanford University), Karthik Narasimhan (Princeton University), Shunyu Yao (Princeton University). Lead author Yitao Liu; corresponding contact lyitao17@gmail.com.
code_url: [uncertain] No official code repository is referenced in the ACL paper or its arXiv version; no public CER repo was located (lead author GitHub: https://github.com/taogoddd, but no CER repo found).
task_domain: LLM-agent sequential decision-making / web navigation (web agents). Text-based web navigation (WebArena) and multimodal/visual web navigation (VisualWebArena). Decision-making / web domain.
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent, training-free (no parameter updates) continual self-improvement of an LLM web-navigation agent at inference time. The agent (a ReAct-style policy built on GPT-4o in BrowserGym) solves multi-step web tasks with a large state/action space and no environment-specific prior knowledge. CER distills reusable experiences (environment dynamics + decision-making skills) from past trajectories into a dynamic in-context memory buffer, retrieves relevant ones for each new task, and 'replays' them in the context window. Three settings are studied, distinguished by the source/time of trajectories: OFFLINE (a fixed training set of trajectories collected in advance via human annotation or LLM self-guided exploration, then frozen), ONLINE (no trajectories initially; the agent learns from its own past-task trajectories during inference, looping distill->retrieve->solve), and HYBRID (offline learning first, then continued online self-evolution). Supervision: ground-truth rewards are NOT required to function (a key claimed advantage over AutoGuide/AutoManual/AWM); CER distills from both successful and failed trajectories. Backbone: GPT-4o-2024-0513 (also tested with Llama-3.1-70B), temperature 0.1, max 30 steps per task.
what_is_retrieved: Distilled experiences of two kinds: (1) environment DYNAMICS - summaries of web pages with their content, inferred possible usages, and corresponding URL (state knowledge enabling state-aware decisions / direct URL navigation); and (2) SKILLS - common decision-making patterns/workflows, each with a brief abstract summary (e.g. 'Navigate to forum {forum name}') plus step-by-step guidelines containing natural-language summaries and concrete action examples. Both are distilled from past (successful and failed) trajectories and stored in the dynamic experience buffer.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING/episodic memory the agent writes itself (with offline and hybrid variants). The retrievable store is a dynamic experience buffer populated by distilling experiences from trajectories: in the online setting it grows at test time from the agent's own past-task trajectories; in the offline setting it is built from a fixed pre-collected trajectory set and then frozen; hybrid combines both. Not a static external corpus (docs/KB/API); it is a self-generated/self-distilled experience memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking objective with a precision flavor: the LLM retriever selects the top-k most useful and informative experiences (capped at k_d=5 dynamics and k_s=5 skills in the WebArena/VisualWebArena implementation), and is explicitly instructed to 'select not more than max skills/pages'. No formal minimal-complete-set recovery objective; selection is a budgeted top-k of the most helpful experiences, not a fixed retrieval ranking benchmark.
retrieval_unit: Two experience-level units: (a) a single environment-dynamics entry = a page summary (page contents + possible usages + URL), and (b) a single skill = a workflow-routine / guideline (sub-goal summary + step-by-step guideline with natural-language steps and concrete action examples). So the retrieved unit is a distilled experience (workflow-routine / guideline-rule / state-summary), not a raw full trajectory.
index_source: Growing memory; construction time varies by setting: online -> online/test-time-induced (buffer grows from self-generated past-task trajectories during inference); offline -> offline-induced and then frozen (built from a pre-collected human-annotated or LLM-explored trajectory set); hybrid -> hybrid (offline-induced then online-grown). Not a static external corpus.
index_structure_topology: Flat experience buffer organized as two separate lists/pools: a dynamics pool (page summaries keyed by content/usage/URL) and a skills pool (workflow guidelines). Selection is done by the LLM reading the task goal, website descriptions, and ALL available dynamics/skills in the buffer (no learned vector index, no graph or explicit hierarchy described; experiences are presented to the model as enumerated id'd items). Effectively metadata/context-keyed flat lists rather than a dense vector index.
retriever_type: LLM-as-retriever: a VLM (GPT-4o) is prompted with the task goal, website descriptions, and all dynamics/skills in the buffer, and outputs the top-k useful experience ids to retrieve. Separate retrieval prompts for dynamics and for skills (Figs. 5-6). Not BM25/dense-embedding-based; selection is performed by the language model itself.
retriever_learning_signal: none (off-the-shelf / prompted): the retrieval module is an un-finetuned GPT-4o prompted to pick the most useful experiences for the current task goal. There is no contrastive training, no LM-feedback fine-tuning, no Bradley-Terry/preference learning, and no RL-trained retrieval policy; retrieval relevance is judged zero-shot by the LLM via instructions in the retrieval prompt.
query_construction: The query is the current task's goal plus the website descriptions, passed (as natural language) to the LLM retrieval module, which breaks the task into a few steps and selects pages/skills helpful for each step. No embedding query; intent is decomposed by the retriever LLM (the retrieval prompt instructs it to 'break the task down into a few steps and then select pages/skills').
query_granularity: task-level (one-shot at t=0): retrieval is performed once per new task, conditioned on the task goal, before solving; the retrieved dynamics/skills are replayed into the context for that whole task. (The retriever internally decomposes the task into steps to choose experiences, but the retrieval call itself is task-level, not per-step re-retrieval.)
when_to_retrieve: one-shot: for each new task, CER runs the retrieval+replay module once (after any distillation from prior trajectories) and augments the context before the agent acts. No iterative/uncertainty-triggered or learned-router mid-episode retrieval is described.
retrieval_trigger_signal: fixed schedule: retrieval is triggered unconditionally at the start of every new task (the buffer is queried, top-k dynamics/skills are selected and injected). There is no token-confidence, attention/uncertainty, learned-complexity-classifier, reflection-token, or agent-initiated mid-episode trigger.
reranking: None as a separate stage. The single LLM-as-retriever pass simultaneously filters and selects the top-k useful experiences; there is no downstream cross-encoder, RRF, or instruction-tuned reranker applied after retrieval.
retrieved_context_refinement: Refinement happens primarily at DISTILLATION/write time rather than post-retrieval: experiences are distilled into abstract, generalized form (e.g. 'navigate to forum {forum name}' with variable placeholders), de-duplicated against existing buffer entries to avoid repetitive distillation, and split into dynamics vs skills. At retrieval, the LLM selects/filters the most useful top-k (a relevance-filtering step). Selected structured experiences are then programmatically mapped (f) into natural-language descriptions before injection. No compression or reason-in-documents distillation of fetched items beyond this selection + format mapping.
how_retrieved_used: prompt augmentation (in-context replay): the k selected experiences E={E_1,...,E_k} are transformed via a programmatic mapping f into natural-language experience descriptions E_NL=f(E), then integrated into the model context C via g, yielding an augmented context C'=g(C,E_NL). The underlying ReAct decision policy then conditions on these replayed dynamics/skills to issue better actions. No fine-tuning or latent-token injection; everything is textual in-context learning.
planning_integration: retrieve-then-plan with one-shot exemplars at plan/task time: for each task CER retrieves and injects relevant dynamics + skills into the ReAct agent's context, after which the agent runs its normal multi-step ReAct (think-act-observe) loop (max 30 steps). Experiences guide both state navigation (dynamics, incl. direct URL goto) and action selection (skills). No MCTS/tree search inside CER itself (though it is shown to compose with a sampling+reranking 'single-turn tree search' surrogate). Retrieval is task-level, not interleaved per planning step.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-answer (per-task/per-episode): retrieval and experience replay occur once before the ReAct rollout for a task; the injected dynamics/skills stay fixed across the multi-step reasoning/acting of that episode. Not per-CoT-step, per-sentence/token, or per-tool-call.
retrieved_item_representation: Distilled free-text experience descriptions injected into the system prompt: (a) environment-dynamics entries formatted as 'Dynamics i: <page name> / contents / potential usages / URL', and (b) skill entries formatted as 'Skill i: <name> / Steps:' with natural-language steps interleaved with concrete executable action examples (e.g. click(id), fill(id, text), goto(url)). So a structured-note / free-text-workflow representation containing both NL summaries and concrete action snippets (not raw trajectories, not latent tokens).
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Distilled, abstract/generalized: experiences are explicitly required to be abstract and broadly applicable (variables/placeholders like {forum name} instead of literal values). Two complementary abstraction types - state-aware environment dynamics (page/state knowledge + URLs) and reusable decision-making skills/workflows (sub-goal-level procedures with step guidelines). Higher abstraction than raw trajectories; the paper argues (cross-template SR) that improvement comes from fine-grained generalizable experiences, not memorized whole trajectories.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Several: (1) Robustness to noisy/incorrect trajectories is shown empirically (Sec. 5.6 / Table 7): CER distills from both successful and failed trajectories and still beats the baseline; using ground-truth-filtered success-only (CER_success) gives only a modest gain (33.5 vs 31.4 avg), evidencing tolerance to noisy experiences, credited to the LLM's implicit reasoning and the flexible natural-language representation. (2) The retrieval LLM filters out useful experiences for the current task (relevance selection). (3) De-duplication at distillation avoids redundant/repetitive experiences. (4) Abstraction/generalization of experiences reduces overfitting to specific tasks.
memory_type: Workflow/procedural + episodic-derived semantic memory: a dynamic experience buffer holding distilled environment dynamics (state/semantic knowledge of pages) and skills (procedural workflows). It is an abstracted experience memory (not raw episodic trajectories, not a skill-program library of executable code, not a graph).
write_back: Yes. The distillation module D writes new distilled experiences (dynamics + skills) into the dynamic buffer epsilon. In online/hybrid settings, after completing each task the agent distills experiences from the just-finished trajectory and merges them into the buffer; in offline, distillation from the pre-collected trajectory set populates the buffer once.
online_growth: Yes in online and hybrid settings: the buffer grows at test/inference time from self-generated past-task trajectories (loop between distillation stage B and inference stage C). In the pure offline setting the buffer is built from a fixed training trajectory set and then frozen (no growth during inference).
write_back_trigger: on-success-and-failure, per-task (reflective distillation): after each completed task (online/hybrid) or for each trajectory in the offline set, the distillation module distills dynamics and skills and merges them into the buffer. Writes occur regardless of success/failure (CER does NOT require ground-truth reward to write); the model is shown existing buffer experiences to avoid repetitive distillation. Not per-step and not human-validated (human only supplies optional offline trajectories).
failure_experience_usage: Success+failure used together: CER explicitly distills fine-grained skills and environment dynamics from BOTH successful and failed trajectories (a stated contribution and a contrast with reward-dependent prior work). Ablation (Table 7) shows the success-only variant CER_success (using ground-truth evaluators to keep only successful trajectories) is only slightly better (33.5 vs 31.4 average), so distillation from failed cases is not a bottleneck and failures contribute useful dynamics/skills. Failures are not stored as separate corrective negative rules; they are mined for reusable dynamics/skills like successes.
memory_evolution_update: Append-and-merge with de-duplication: new distilled experiences are merged into the buffer continually across time, and the distillation model is provided the existing buffer to avoid repetitive/duplicate distillation (so it appends genuinely new dynamics/skills rather than rewriting all). The paper contrasts CER with Agent Workflow Memory, which rewrites the whole workflow memory; CER instead continuously merges new experiences (incremental append/merge rather than full-overwrite). No explicit forget/prune or per-entry refine-overwrite mechanism is described.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Case/experience selection is performed by a prompted (un-finetuned) GPT-4o acting as the retriever; it is not an RL-/value-optimized or contrastively-trained retrieval policy. (Selection is LLM-judged top-k rather than fixed embedding top-k, but it is not a learned policy in the trained-parameters sense.)
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent private memory: one agent accumulates and replays its own distilled experience buffer. The paper does show generalization across task templates and compatibility/composition with other off-the-shelf agent methods (e.g. sampling+reranking 'tree search' surrogate), but not memory sharing across multiple agents or heterogeneous frameworks.
benchmarks: WebArena (Zhou et al. 2024b; 812 tasks across 5 sites/domains: Shopping, Shopping Admin/CMS, Forum/Reddit, Gitlab, Map) and VisualWebArena (Koh et al. 2024a; 910 multimodal tasks across Classifieds, Shopping, Forum). Environment: BrowserGym (Drouin et al. 2024), with Set-of-Marks (SoM) image annotation for VisualWebArena. Backbones: GPT-4o-2024-0513 (main), Llama-3.1-70B (open-source validation on the Gitlab split).
benchmark_family: web (WebArena; VisualWebArena - realistic interactive web navigation / multimodal web agents).
baselines: GPT-4o w/ BrowserGym (ReAct-format) reproduced by the authors as the primary comparable baseline; WebArena original agent (Zhou et al. 2024b); AutoEval (Pan et al. 2024); VisualWebArena original agent (Koh et al. 2024a); Tree Search (Koh et al. 2024b) on VisualWebArena; SteP (Sodhi et al. 2024) listed for reference only (uses human-designed per-website policies, not autonomous, so excluded from fair comparison). For synergy: trajectory sampling + reranking (a single-turn surrogate of Tree Search). For open-source: ReAct baseline with Llama-3.1-70B. Related-work contrasts: ExpeL, Synapse, Voyager, Generative Agents, Learn-by-interact, AutoGuide, AutoManual, Agent Workflow Memory (AWM).
key_metrics: Task success rate (SR, %) overall and per website/domain; relative SR improvement over baseline; cross-template success rate (ct-SR); stability (% of baseline-solved tasks retained) and plasticity (% additional tasks solved vs baseline); token efficiency (Delta input tokens, Delta tokens %, Delta SR %).
headline_result: On WebArena, CER_hybrid reaches 36.7% average SR, relatively improving the GPT-4o w/ BrowserGym baseline (24.3%) by 51.0% (per-site: Shopping 32.8, CMS 41.2, Forum 41.2, Gitlab 37.2, Map 30.4). On VisualWebArena, CER_online reaches 31.9% average SR (Classifieds 27.0, Shopping 38.1, Forum 24.4), outperforming the Tree Search method (26.4%) by ~20.8% relative with dozens-of-times fewer token costs. CER offline/online/hybrid on WebArena = 33.4 / 33.2 / 36.7 average SR.
ablations: (1) Token efficiency (Table 3): vs ReAct baseline (24.3 SR), CER adds only +5.8% / +11.2% / +17.3% input tokens for offline/online/hybrid while raising SR by +37.8% / +36.7% / +52.5% relative - large gains for minor token overhead. (2) Cross-template SR / stability & plasticity (Table 4, Forum): CER ct-SR 60.0 vs baseline 44.7, stability 93%, plasticity 141% (41% new task types solved), showing improvement comes from generalizable fine-grained experiences, not memorizing whole trajectories. (3) Open-source model (Table 5, Gitlab, Llama-3.1-70B): CER_hybrid 22.0 vs ReAct 17.3 (~+26.5% relative; smaller gain than GPT-4o, attributed to weaker formatting/skill distillation). (4) Synergy (Table 6, Forum): CER 37.7, Sampling 43.1, CER w/ sampling 52.6 (+39.5% over CER w/ ReAct) - composes with performant methods. (5) Robustness / success-only (Table 7, full WebArena): CER 31.4 vs CER_success 33.5 - distilling from failed trajectories is not a bottleneck; robust to noisy trajectories. (6) Division of dynamics vs skills (Table 8, Forum): CER 37.7 vs CER-skills 33.3 vs CER-dynamics 35.1 - both components matter and synergize. (7) Offline data source (Table 9, Forum): human annotations vs self-guided exploration; human-annotated offline (33.3) and hybrid (41.2) beat exploration-based (offline 31.6, hybrid 35.1), and hybrid w/ human annotations (41.2) surpasses online-only (37.7); noisy unstructured exploration trajectories can mislead, showing goal-oriented trajectories matter.
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end task SR (and derived ct-SR/stability/plasticity/token metrics) are reported; no intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / retrieval completeness) are reported separately, since retrieval here is LLM-judged experience selection for in-context replay rather than a ranked-retrieval benchmark.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome (success rate / reward). Some process-oriented analyses are reported: cross-template SR (generalization), stability vs plasticity (knowledge retention vs acquisition), token-cost analysis, and qualitative case study (e.g. WebArena task 31 showing how distilled dynamics+skills enable correct navigation/sorting). No formal step-wise reasoning-faithfulness or trajectory-quality metric.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: A central selling point: CER adds only modest input-token overhead (Delta tokens +5.8% offline / +11.2% online / +17.3% hybrid) for large relative SR gains (+37.8% / +36.7% / +52.5%) (Table 3). On VisualWebArena it beats Tree Search (which samples 20x at each step over up to 5 steps with GPT-4o as a value function) using a max of only 30 steps per task and 'at least 3 times fewer tokens' (text says 'dozens of times fewer token costs' relative to the search budget). No explicit dollar/latency figures.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed/budget-capped top-k: in the WebArena & VisualWebArena implementation, k_d=5 (max dynamics) and k_s=5 (max skills) are retrieved/replayed; retrieval prompts explicitly cap selection ('select not more than max skills/pages'). Experiences are kept abstract/compact and the added tokens are small (single-digit to ~17% of input). Selection count is fixed-k (not adaptive/precision-driven beyond the cap), retrieved-then-injected.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing benchmarks: WebArena 812 tasks / 5 sites; VisualWebArena 910 tasks / 3 sites). Offline training trajectories were newly collected: ~5-10 human-annotated gold tasks per WebArena website (~5% of test set, filtered to avoid test overlap), or alternatively 10 LLM self-guided exploration trajectories (max 30 steps each).
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve: yes (LLM-as-retriever selects top-k relevant dynamics/skills per task), Reuse: yes (experiences replayed in context to guide ReAct decisions), Revise: partial (experiences are distilled/abstracted and de-duplicated at write time; retrieved experiences themselves are reused as-is without per-case solution adaptation at solve time), Retain: yes (distilled experiences merged into the dynamic buffer, growing online)].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper frames itself via experience replay (citing Lin-style replay, Schaul et al. Prioritized Experience Replay 2016, Rolnick et al. 2019 experience replay for continual learning) and the Recognition-Primed Decision model (Klein 1998); it does NOT cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner or use the term case-based reasoning. It realizes CBR-like Retrieve/Reuse/Retain mechanisms under an experience-replay / continual-learning / self-improvement framing.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (not a tool-retrieval method; web actions are issued via BrowserGym action space, e.g. click/fill/goto, not a retrievable tool/API index).
index_content_separation: Partial: experiences are stored as structured entries (dynamics: name+contents+usages+URL; skills: name+steps) and only the selected top-k are programmatically expanded into natural-language descriptions and loaded into context at solve time, so a lightweight selectable index is separated from on-demand full content (akin to a shortcut-list-then-content pattern). Not a formal SOP-index-then-content design.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (not a tool-retrieval system; environment interaction is via the BrowserGym web action API / accessibility tree, not RapidAPI/RESTful/MCP/function-calling tool stores).
adaptation_mechanism: Verbatim in-context replay with LLM-prompted generalization at distillation rather than per-case solve-time adaptation: retrieved dynamics/skills are injected as-is (after programmatic NL formatting) and the ReAct policy adapts them implicitly via reasoning. The 'adaptation' is front-loaded into distillation, where the LLM abstracts experiences with variable placeholders so they apply broadly; no execution-feedback-driven revision of a retrieved case at solve time.
builds_on: ReAct (Yao et al. 2023b, base think-act-observe policy and output format) and BrowserGym (Drouin et al. 2024, web environment/observation); experience replay for RL/continual learning (Lin; Schaul et al. 2016 Prioritized Experience Replay; Rolnick et al. 2019); memory/experience LLM agents (Generative Agents - Park et al. 2023; Voyager - Wang et al. 2024a; ExpeL - Zhao et al. 2023; Synapse - Zheng et al. 2023); Set-of-Marks visual grounding (Yang et al. 2023); Recognition-Primed Decision model (Klein 1998); benchmarks WebArena (Zhou et al. 2024b) and VisualWebArena (Koh et al. 2024a).
contrasts_with: Methods requiring ground-truth reward to function before learning - AutoGuide (Fu et al. 2024), AutoManual (Chen et al. 2024), Agent Workflow Memory/AWM (Wang et al. 2024b) - CER works without ground-truth rewards and from both success and failure; AWM specifically lacks a retrieval module and rewrites the whole workflow memory, whereas CER retrieves and continually merges. Methods that store raw long observation-action pairs as exemplars (ExpeL, Synapse) - CER instead distills fine-grained, abstract dynamics/skills better suited to complex environments. Compute-heavy search methods (Tree Search, Koh et al. 2024b) - CER is much cheaper in tokens. SteP (Sodhi et al. 2024) - relies on human-designed per-website policies (not autonomous). Parameter-update/training-based agent learning - CER is training-free.
lineage: Group D (case-based / experience planning): a training-free, in-context experience-replay LLM web agent in the lineage of experience/insight-memory agents (ReAct -> Reflexion/ExpeL -> Agent Workflow Memory -> CER). It advances test-time continual self-improvement by distilling environment dynamics + decision-making skills from both successful and failed trajectories into a dynamic in-context buffer (write-back + LLM-as-retriever replay), without ground-truth reward and without parameter updates, validated on realistic web-navigation benchmarks.
